author: haiku
label: pilot-junior-fix-01
changes: Added the rollback_in_progress flag and a note on how workers learn to stop charging during freeze, since billing_mode stays at its pre-rollback value until hand off (answers Q5).
Replaced the Halted to Freeze edge with one resume edge per step, labelled as resuming the recorded failed step, and added a failure edge from Hand_off_to_old_engine to Halted (answers Q8).

Renamed the diagram's human-move and on-call labels to say which check the controller runs and that on-call sends a request to the controller, and added the day-35 condition that no rollback is in progress (answers Q1, Q2, Q10).
Added a Human moves and gate checks section describing how the controller verifies each gate before writing billing_mode and the gate record together (answers Q2).
Added per-source-mode notes for rollback from shadow, both and new_only, so the no-op steps and the shadow-only data are explicit (answers Q6).
Defined settled, the ledger role and the idempotency key in Where rollout state lives (answers Q7).
Stated Finance sign-off storage and withdrawal in the failure section and listed signer authority as open (answers Q4).

Added failure rules for hand off and the 2 percent trigger minimum, and expanded the open questions to cover the failure-rate measurement, the usage event log writer, the day-35 rollback case and the ledger schema (answers Q3, Q9, Q10).
Kept the brief's rules unchanged: the mode order, gate numbers, 2 percent trigger, 35-day limit, and the no-double-charge rule.

Q11: replaced my invented rule that any mismatch resets the shadow streak with the brief's per-day rate gate (mismatches divided by invoices compared, strictly under 0.1 percent). Defined mismatch, mismatch rate and a counted day, and noted that days with 1,000 or fewer invoices fail on any mismatch.
Q12: the nightly job writes only per-date results; the controller updates the gate record, keyed by date to avoid double-counting; days in both come from both_entered_at, removing one counter.

Q13 and Q14: added a single charging rule (old engine when billing_mode is old_only or shadow; new engine when billing_mode is both or new_only with no rollback flag, failing closed if the gate record is unreadable). It replaces the blanket claim that charging of due periods stays paused, which was wrong for shadow.
Q14: catch-up is defined as compute and write to the ledger with no charges.
Q16: added single-rollback rules for start, resume, other requests, automatic triggers and human moves during a rollback.
Q15: day-35 mechanics defined: entry time written with billing_mode, fixed 35x24-hour duration, enforced at request time, the daily job only records closure.
Rollback wording: from both or new_only the rollback goes straight to old_only, not through shadow. The earlier phrase 'may skip modes' was unclear.
Per-source charging notes in the rollback steps were restated to match the single charging rule.
Gate record fields now include rollback_source and new_only_entered_at, and the hand-off reset now clears the Finance sign-off and the new_only entry time.

Failure section: a gate-record outage now stops new-engine charging. Withdrawing sign-off after the move to new_only is stated to have no effect on the mode. The rollback-step and hand-off failure text now follows the charging rule.
Assumptions added: a day with no invoices does not count, a one-sided invoice is a mismatch, and a non-counting day breaks the consecutive run. The 35-day limit is stated to apply only to new_only.

Open questions: added that billing_mode and the gate record sit in two stores with no shared transaction, and that a billing period straddling the new_only entry time is not handled. Removed the counter and day-35 questions now decided. The day-35 rollback question stays open, with its risk stated.
The Mermaid diagram was left unchanged.

Commit order: removed the 'one versioned change' claim for human moves and hand off, and defined a fixed write order (gate first with pending_mode for forward moves; config first for hand off), with recovery after a partial write. Why: Q18, the two stores share no transaction.

Gate record: added pending_mode, rollback_status (running or halted) and catch_up_cursor. Corrected the billing_mode writers to a forward move and hand off only, since rollback start writes no billing_mode. Why: Q17 and Q18.
Rollback: the controller executes all steps, records rollback_step before and after each step, and resumes the recorded step after a crash. Why: Q17.
Drain: defined the outcome for each provider answer (charged, not charged, unknown) and the wait-then-halt rule for unknown outcomes. Why: Q19.
Catch-up: defined scope (no overwrite of existing ledger invoices, differences recorded), trigger, cursor and completion. Why: Q20.
Daily comparison: defined the comparison scope by period end date in UTC, and the complete test. Why: Q21.
Failures: gate outage now states that the old engine in shadow does not depend on the gate record, and that nothing charges in both or new_only during an outage. Why: Q22.
Charging: added the intent row (conditional insert keyed by customer-period) and a key derived only from customer ID and billing period ID. The ledger check now includes intent rows. Why: Q23.

Hand-off failure: after step 1 succeeds the old engine may charge, since steps 1 to 4 have finished and the new engine is still stopped by the flag. This replaces the earlier 'does not charge until hand off succeeds' wording. Why: consistency with the commit order.

Day 35: the new_only clock starts at the gate write that records new_only_entered_at, which is no later than the mode change. Closure now also requires no pending_mode. Automatic triggers at or after day 35 are refused too, to match the diagram. Why: the commit order and the diagram.

Open questions: added the step 1 acknowledgement, provider handling of repeated keys, the unknown-outcome timeout, the config compare-and-set question, the billing period definition, the catch-up deadline against 35-day event expiry, charge-failure handling after day 35, the gate-outage stop in both and new_only, and catch-up differences blocking hand-off. Why: these are holes the answers depend on and do not yet resolve.
Who may charge: the new engine now inserts its intent row first and then reads rollback_in_progress, so an engine that saw the flag clear has always left a row the freeze step can find (Q26).

Controller step 1 (freeze): completion is now defined as a scan of intent rows after the flag write, which removes the unexplained 'how is this learned' gap; the cross-store read order is listed as open (Q26).

Controller step 3: rewritten as a verify step. Intent rows are the only source of charged periods, the provider answer per key drives settlement, and missing settled entries are written; the earlier reconcile wording did not say where charges were found (Q25).
Commit order: old_only to shadow is now a forward move with pending_mode, streak reset and shadow_started_at written before billing_mode, so the first move has a defined write order (Q24).
Gate record and assumptions: added shadow_started_at, and dates before it do not count, since the new engine had produced no output for them (Q24).

Daily comparison: the nightly job now writes one mismatch record per mismatched customer-period as well as the count row. The earlier 'writes nothing else' made the 14-day gate unreadable, and the gate now counts open mismatch records (Q27).
Starting and requests: the automatic trigger is evaluated by the controller itself, with rollback_source recorded as on_call:<requester> or automatic:charge_failure_rate (Q29).
Added a section on hand off after its first write: the old engine's intended charging, idempotent resume, and the refusals that apply during this window (Q28).
Failure section: an unreadable gate record leaves intent rows pending, which blocks both engines until drain, and a failed comparison date now blocks the 14-day gate until re-run (Q26, Q27).

Open questions: added the cross-store read order, the provider answer format, the incomplete-day gap in the 14-day gate, and who may resolve mismatches, with the ledger-invoice problem in both (Q25, Q26, Q27).

Diagram: the automatic trigger label now says it is the controller's, and the shadow-to-both and old_only moves are labelled with their gate or reset. The Verify_ledger node replaces Reconcile_ledger to match the step rename.
Charge intent: added the normal-path settlement rule (the charging engine writes the settled entry, retries on failure, and the controller resolves a stuck row by key). Answers Q30.
Charge intent: defined a due customer-period as a ledger invoice with no settled entry, and listed the due trigger and worker location as open. Answers Q31.
What happens when something fails: added a stale billing_mode read case. The intent row prevents a second charge, but not a charge by the wrong engine. Answers Q32.
Daily comparison: a non-counting day now resets shadow_streak_days and shadow_streak_invoices together, and the 5,000 total counts only the current run. Answers Q33.
Daily comparison: the nightly job writes mismatch records before the count row, and the controller reads only dates with a count row. Answers Q34.
Charge intent: an engine charges the unsettled ledger invoice amount and never overwrites one, which also fixes what the old engine charges after hand off from both. Answers Q35.

Charge intent and drain: added a charge deadline, and drain clears a row as not charged only after it has passed, so a late provider call cannot follow a 'not charged' answer. Answers Q36. Its length is open.

Open questions: added the due trigger and worker location, billing_mode read cadence, nightly job schedule, outside-rollback resolution timing, the charge deadline, and the review of ledger-versus-engine differences after hand off.

Who may charge: added a flag pre-check before the intent insert for the new engine (step 0), so frozen workers stop creating rows. The post-insert flag read is unchanged, and it carries the freeze argument. Reason: Q39.
Who may charge and Charge intent: intent rows now record the inserting engine, as metadata outside the key, to scope the rollback steps. Reason: Q40.

Controller step 1: the scan is one ledger query for unsettled new-engine intent rows, run after the flag write, and it is the drain set. Rows inserted after the query by flag-set workers are picked up by step 2. Reason: Q39.

Controller step 2: drain repeats until no unsettled new-engine rows remain. A not-charged answer younger than the charge deadline keeps the row pending and is re-asked on a later pass, tracked by rollback_step and the ledger insert time. Reason: Q38, Q39.
Controller step 3: verification covers only the drain set, so old-engine rows do not block hand off. Reason: Q40.

Per source mode: From shadow, the old engine keeps charging and its rows follow the normal path. From both, old-engine rows left from an earlier shadow phase are resolved by normal controller resolution. Reason: Q40.
Rollback start: added rollback_from_mode to the gate write and the gate record. Reason: Q37, so per-source handling knows the mode after a pending move.
New section Rollback start while a forward move is pending: the pending move completes first, then the rollback starts, and the exposure is stated. Reason: Q37.
Starting and requests: a start request or automatic trigger during a pending move is held until the move completes. Reason: Q37.

Charge deadline: measured from the ledger insert timestamp, with a provider-latency margin before a not-charged answer is final. Reason: Q38, which exposed that the deadline could not be checked without a clock source.
What happens when something fails: added the not-charged-younger-than-deadline case and the held rollback request during a config outage. Reason: Q37, Q38.
Open questions: added the pass interval, deadline length and latency bound, the pending-move exposure, and the consistency of the step 1 query. Reason: Q37, Q38, Q39.
holes: Q1: Who is 'on-call' and how do they trigger a rollback or a resume: a CLI command, a button, a ticket? Does the rollout controller receive it? (author: The brief does not say how on-call starts a rollback (CLI command, button or ticket). The document now says on-call sends a rollback request to the rollout controller, and that the controller is the only writer of billing_mode. The mechanism is listed as an open question.)

Q3: How is the automatic trigger measured: who computes the new-engine charge failure rate per 10-minute window, from what data, and who tells the controller to start rollback? (author: The brief does not say who computes the automatic 2 percent trigger or from what data, and it gives no minimum charge count per 10-minute window. A proposal (the new engine emits each charge outcome and the controller computes the rate per window) is written in the document as an open question, not as settled design.)

Q9: What is the 'usage events' log, who writes it and what is the 35-day retention? What exactly does the old engine do when it 'skips' events in new_only? (author: The brief does not say who writes the usage event log. It does give the 35-day retention. The document says the old engine, in new_only, does not compute from the events, so the events stay in the log. Catch-up reads the retained events from the start of new_only and writes their invoices to the ledger, skipping periods already settled. Writer and exact retention behaviour are open.)

Q10: The diagram says automatic rollback in new_only is allowed before day 35, but what happens if a rollback is in progress or Halted when day 35 arrives? (author: The brief does not say what happens to a rollback that is in progress or Halted on day 35. The document now says the day-35 closure fires only from new_only with no rollback in progress. Charging stays paused and nothing returns to old_only until a person decides. Whether an earlier rollback may finish catch-up after day 35 is open.)

Q31: What makes a customer-period 'due', and what starts an engine's attempt to charge it (a schedule, an event, a polling loop)? Where do the workers run? (author: The brief does not say what makes a customer-period due, what starts an engine's charge attempt (schedule, event or polling loop), or where the workers run. The document now defines due as a ledger invoice with no settled entry, which the catch-up rule already relies on. The trigger and the worker location are listed as open questions.)

Q32: How and how often do workers read billing_mode (per charge, cached, pushed)? How stale can their value be around a mode switch, and what keeps two engines from charging then? (author: The brief does not give how often workers read billing_mode, whether they cache it, or how stale it can be. The document does not depend on these for no double charge: the intent row stops a second charge to the same customer-period whichever engine reads a stale mode. A stale read can still let the wrong engine charge in a mode, so that is now listed under what happens when something fails. The staleness bound is open.)

Q36: After drain clears an intent row as not charged, can a late call from the new engine, which already read the flag clear, still reach the provider with the same key? How is that handled? (author: This was a real gap. The new engine can read the flag as clear, insert its row, and send the charge after drain has already asked the provider and been told no charge exists. The provider's idempotency key does not stop a first request that arrives late. The document now says drain may clear a row as not charged only after a charge deadline has passed since the row was inserted, and that an engine must not send a provider call for a row older than that deadline. The deadline length, and whether the provider's answer is final after it, are not known and are listed as open questions.)
